newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KGHM '96 gross profit down,copper output up.
newsitem.headline: Polish KGHM '96 gross profit down,copper output up.

text.p: Poland's KGHM Polska Miedz SA pre-tax profit is expected to be around 500 million zlotys in 1996, down from 836 million zlotys in 1995, as lower copper prices on world markets trimmed the concern's profits.

KGHM president Stanislaw Siwierski told Rzeczpospolita business daily that the concern's copper production increased by 20,000 tonnes last year to 425,000 tonnes while its silver output fell to 933 tonnes from 964 tonnes in 1995.
Its gold output increased to 530 kg from 474 kg in 1995.
KGHM, expected to float part of its shares around mid-year, cut its costs by around five percent in 1996, Siwierski said.

He also said KGHM, worth an estimated $1.5 to $3 billion, would continue to shed non-core activities in 1997, cutting its emplOyment to 23,400 people by the end of the year from 28,000 at the start of 1996.
This restructuring process is aimed at cutting KGHM's labour force to about 20,000 workers directly employed in the production cycle, by the year 2000, Rzeczpospolita said.
Siwierski said KGHM's privatisation could not be stopped despite some political pressure to delay the sell-off until after parliamentary elections, expected after August 1997.

"Privatisation of Polska Miedz lies in the interest of the state treasury. It will increase the firm's prestige and give ways to raise new capital, which is still needed by the firm," Siwierski was quoted as saying.

Under the goverment's tentative privatisation plan, the treasury will cut its stake in KGHM to 49 percent. About 36 percent of shares will be offered in London and Warsaw bourses and to 15 percent of shares will to KGHM employees free.
KGHM plans to increase its copper output to 470,000 tonnes annually by 2000, while raising its silver output to 1,000 tonnes and gold to 1,000 kg.
